headline: Braves rout Phillies 12-2 behind eight-run fourth
recap: The Phillies were routed 12-2 by the Atlanta Braves on Saturday night at Truist Park, undone by an eight-run fourth inning. Bryce Harper's leadoff homer in the first, his 28th of the season, gave Philadelphia an early 1-0 lead, but Ronald Acuña Jr. tied it with a home run off Brooks Raley in the bottom of the fourth; Raley recorded only two outs and was charged with the loss. Reliever Grant Holman couldn't stop the bleeding that followed: a two-run single by Mauricio Dubón, an unearned run that scored when Sean Murphy reached on a fielding error by third baseman Bryson Stott, a bases-clearing double by Drake Baldwin, and an RBI single by Acuña turned the tie game into an 8-1 Atlanta lead. Ozzie Albies added a sacrifice fly off Chase Shugart in the sixth to make it 9-1. In the eighth, Justin Crawford hit a solo homer, his third of the season, before Michael Harris II answered with a three-run homer off position player Garrett Stubbs in the bottom half for the final 12-2 margin. Tyler Mahle worked seven innings for the win, allowing only Harper's homer.
The loss was Philadelphia's third straight. The Phillies are 82-67, second in the NL East, six games behind the division-leading Braves.

Philadelphia closes out the series in Atlanta this afternoon, with first pitch at Truist Park scheduled for 1:35 PM ET. Andrew Painter starts for the Phillies opposite Grant Holmes for the Braves. The Braves are favored at -137 on the moneyline, with the Phillies at +113.
